quotes.text: Customers new to Link can save their payment details and shipping information to enable faster checkout in the future.
Trigger Link in the Payment Element whenever a customer selects a supported payment method.
Display Link alongside Apple Pay, Google Pay, and PayPal using the Express Checkout Element.
Use the Contact Details Element to create an email input field that authenticates Link customers.
The Payment Request Button is deprecated.

old_evidence.text: Create a single email input for both email collection and Link authentication.
The `onChange` handler fires when a user updates the email field or Link autofills a saved customer email.

findings: The November 7 capture turns the canonical URL into a Link with Web Elements overview for one-click custom checkout. It explicitly names saving payment and shipping information for new Link customers, recommended Payment Element triggering on selection of a supported payment method, recommended Express Checkout Element showing Link alongside Apple Pay, Google Pay and PayPal, Contact Details Element email authentication, deprecated Payment Request Button migration to Express Checkout Element, and the Card Element save/autofill route (new raw lines 5-21).

The May 8 capture covers the standalone Link Authentication Element. Pass a known email directly to the Payment Element when appropriate. For new users the sign-up prompt follows selection of a supported credit card, debit card or US bank account. A returning user receives a phone OTP, after which successful authentication permits saved payment and address autofill. The guide requires domain registration, uses a PaymentIntent client secret, makes the Address Element optional for shipping, and documents optional email prefill and email change events (old raw lines 6-50 and 54-128).

The mapped source lines 13-44 captures most of the May behaviors but needs historical and API scope, the omitted known-email alternative, the correct React identifiers, and a November overview. Capturing or autofilling contact data, displaying a wallet, or authenticating a Link customer is distinct from confirming, capturing or settling a payment.
substantive_changes: The canonical document changes from a single component how-to to a multi-path Link Web Elements recommendation page, with explicit trigger, co-display, authentication and save/autofill descriptions plus a deprecated integration's migration target (old raw lines 1-50, new raw lines 5-21). The route targets and supported-method phrasing carry integration-selection guidance even where their implementation bodies sit elsewhere.

Contact Details Element replaces the historical component name in the overview. Dated May 27 evidence attributes the name change and continued JavaScript alias support to the Dahlia changelog. The November page provides no evidence of a new cutoff or a behavior change. The more detailed Contact Details guide separately preserves domain registration, standard Elements client-secret setup, optional Address Element ordering, one-render multi-step guidance and an onChange email event.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep the May 8 PaymentIntent implementation with known-email alternative, supported signup methods, OTP then autofill, domain registration, optional Address placement between authentication and Payment Element, vanilla create/mount and React provider contexts, optional prefilled email and loader, and dated multi-page/onChange behavior (old raw lines 6-50 and 54-128). The old filename does not give the capture year.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/elements-link, the November page describes one-click Link checkout in Web Elements and saving payment and shipping details for new Link customers. It recommends triggering Link on a supported Payment Element selection or displaying it in Express Checkout Element beside Apple Pay, Google Pay and PayPal. Contact Details Element uses the email field for authentication, Payment Request Button is deprecated and routes existing Link integrations to Express Checkout migration, and Card Element remains a save and autofill route (new raw lines 5-21). The May 8 guide summarized by source-stripe-elements-link.md was a standalone PaymentIntent Link Authentication Element how-to. It uses a client secret and registered domain, optionally takes a default email, recommends passing an already known email to Payment Element, places Address Element between the authentication and payment components when needed, and documents supported sign-up choices, phone OTP followed by saved-data autofill, and React input/autofilled email change events (old raw lines 6-50 and old raw lines 54-128). The mapped summary keeps most historical behavior, but it lacks the November scope and carries lowercase React JSX. These client flows and email events provide no proof of confirmation or capture.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/elements-link, the shortened how-to and new destination links are structural, while the two preferred paths, their trigger and display behavior, the renamed authentication route and Payment Request Button migration affect integration choices (new raw lines 9-21). In source-stripe-elements-link.md preserve the dated setup, supported signup choices, successful OTP prerequisite, registered domain, optional shipping order and single-render, email prefill and change-handler behavior (old raw lines 6-50 and old raw lines 54-128). Link the historical and present routes reciprocally. The May 27 Dahlia rename preserves the documented behavior and both Stripe.js creation strings without requiring existing integrations to change. Correct lowercase React JSX with version-scoped public component identifiers and keep beta LinkSignupElement separate. The dated Checkout Sessions addition links to 2026-05-27.dahlia and uses Contact Details Element for email collection, validation and Link sign-in. Scope the historical sample to standard Elements and PaymentIntents and keep API entrypoint and package claims within their specific evidence. Assign deprecation and migration to Payment Request Button. The listed Card Element route still supports the documented save and autofill behavior, with separate guidance preferring other Elements. The overview does not establish any change in runtime behavior, provider compatibility, or completed payment.
